Figure 2:Curation and composition of3DCodeVerse-2M.Left: We collect programs from public datasets and generate more with our harness.
Middle: Our 3D coding harness, equipped with modeling skills and inspection tools (e.g., 3D IoU, collision checks), builds each program, judges the output, and refines it until it passes.
Each verified program is paired with rendered images and captions, plus meshes and videos when available.
Right: The resulting corpus covers 3D objects, articulated objects, scenes, and graphics across multiple programming languages and engines.

Figure 3:Overview of the3DCodeVerseHarness.Given an input prompt, an LLM planner defines the target asset, and a DAG coordinates sub-agents to code and assemble a 3D program (left).
Execution checks, spatial measurements, and rubric-guided VLM judgments provide automated feedback (center) for targeted code revisions by a fix agent (bottom).
The right panel illustrates successive refinement rounds, with the highest-scoring program selected as the final output.

Figure 4:Main results of3DCodeVerseHarness across four 3D coding tasks.Panels show (a) 3D objects, (b) articulated objects, (c) scenes, and (d) graphics.
Blue bars report Human Preference (%), and orange bars report Judge Score (0–100; failed generations receive a score of zero).
Hatched bars denote each backbone’s native harness, while solid bars denote3DCodeVerseHarness.
The final group in (a) compares Claude Design with3DCodeVerseHarness, both using Claude Opus 5.5.

Figure 5:Qualitative comparisons and automated refinement.(a)Outputs for identical prompts and backbones using the native harness (Without) versus3DCodeVerseHarness (With).(b)Selected rounds of automated refinement for objects and graphics.
Numbers report rubric scores on a[0,1][0,1]scale and are comparable within each pair or refinement sequence.
Figure 7:Applications.Code renders from our harness guide video generation with Gemini Omni Flash 1.1 for robot manipulation scenes (top) and Seedance 2.5 for a GPT-6 Astra scene (bottom).

Figure 11:Vision–language judgment: evidence payload, structured schema, and score synthesis.The judge inspects structured telemetry and labelled multi-view montages without access to source code or generator reasoning (left); its schema enforces explicit visual observation prior to criterion scoring (middle).
Right: baseline-round score computation for §A.6, combining criterion means, majority-voted defects, and deterministic gate caps.

Figure 12:Recorded trajectoryfor the prompt “a three-legged wooden stool” on the Three.js runtime under the economy profile.
Each column shows one round: the rendered view inspected by the judge, the composite score with its penalties and caps, deterministic gate findings, and VLM defect votes.
Closed-loop refinement resolves all baseline floating and interpenetrating parts in Round 1 (0.410→0.8440.410\to 0.844) and refines geometric detailing in Round 2 (11,05211{,}052triangles, reaching0.9330.933under the strict metric-footprint cap), completing in4.04.0active minutes at $0.74.

Figure 13:Articulated mechanism verification, illustrated on a recorded run for “a laptop with a hinged lid”.
Link geometry is authored in Blender and kinematic structure in URDF; the build verifies rest-pose frame agreement, and the joint sweep articulates the mechanism across its motion limits.
The dynamic sweep automatically detects a subtle2.52.5mm hinge–base collision at the upper opening limit that is invisible at rest, enforcing physical articulability via the rubric cap.

Figure 14:Scene and procedural graphics tracks.(a) Scene generation executes a staged asset-and-zone assembly pipeline before entering the closed-loop refinement cycle with scene-specific gates.
(b) Graphics generation synthesizes fragment shaders or OpenGL programs whose temporal frames are sampled at fixed timestamps, verified by statistical frame gates, and evaluated as multi-frame montages.

Columns show the initial observation, MuJoCo simulation of the generated 3D code, its reconstruction through UWM’s frozen VAE, the static last-frame reference, and all three UWM rollout seeds.
Enlarged2×2\timescrops (dashed boxes) demonstrate that executable 3D code preserves sharp, consistent door and handle geometry both before and after VAE reconstruction, whereas UWM rollouts exhibit seed-dependent contour drift.
